description: Saccharum officinarum: a tall, clumping grass grown for the sugar in its canes.

diseases.name: Sugarcane Mosaic
diseases.pathogen: Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) and related potyviruses
diseases.description: A virus disease that mottles sugarcane leaves with pale green streaks.
diseases.causes: Aphids spread the virus; infected seed cane (setts) carries it into new fields.
symptoms: Pale green to yellow streaks and patches between darker green areas
Most visible at the base of young leaves
diseases.untreated: Infected setts carry it into every new planting.

steps.title: Remove infected stools early
steps.instruction: Dig out mottled plants in young crops.

steps.title: Use healthy seed cane
steps.rationale: The main source of the virus.

steps.title: Control grass weeds
steps.instruction: Remove grass weeds round the field.
steps.rationale: They host the virus and aphids.

lifecycle: Aphids carry the virus to nearby plants.
Pale streaks appear on young leaves.
Infected canes are used as seed and spread it on.
sources: Sugarcane Leaf Disease Dataset (Mendeley Data) class: Mosaic, sugarcane mosaic

diseases.name: Red Rot
diseases.description: The most destructive fungal disease of sugarcane: it rots the inside of the cane red and marks the leaf midribs.
diseases.causes: Spores spread in infected setts, by rain and irrigation water, and through borer holes; waterlogging and susceptible varieties favour it.
symptoms: Long, blood-red lesions along the leaf midrib, later with straw-coloured centres
Upper leaves yellow and dry from the tips
Split canes are red inside with white patches and smell sour
diseases.effect: Infected canes dry out and lose their sugar.
diseases.untreated: Whole fields can be lost with susceptible varieties.

steps.title: Remove and destroy affected clumps
steps.instruction: Dig out infected clumps with their roots and burn or bury them.

steps.title: Improve drainage
steps.instruction: Avoid waterlogging and don't let water run from infected plots.

steps.title: Plant treated, healthy setts of a resistant variety
steps.instruction: Use resistant varieties and treated seed cane next time.

lifecycle: The fungus comes in on infected setts.
Spores spread by water and wind.
Red lesions form on the midribs; canes rot inside.
Canes dry; spores spread to new plantings.

diseases.name: Sugarcane Rust
diseases.pathogen: Puccinia melanocephala (brown rust) and P. kuehnii (orange rust)
diseases.description: Rust fungi that streak sugarcane leaves with brown or orange pustules.
diseases.causes: Spores blow on the wind; warm, humid weather with dew favours infection.
symptoms: Small, elongated yellow flecks on both leaf sides
Flecks grow into brown or orange-brown pustules along the veins
Pustules merge and leaves dry early
diseases.effect: Leaf area falls, reducing growth and sugar.
diseases.untreated: Severe rust can cut yields of susceptible varieties sharply.

steps.title: Scout the leaves
steps.instruction: Check how many leaves carry pustules.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on susceptible varieties on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores blow in on the wind.
Yellow flecks become rust pustules along the veins.
New spores spread across the field.
sources: Sugarcane Leaf Disease Dataset (Mendeley Data) class: Rust, sugarcane rust
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Yellow Leaf Disease
diseases.pathogen: Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV, a polerovirus)
diseases.description: A virus disease that yellows the midrib of sugarcane leaves and stunts the canes.
diseases.causes: Aphids (the sugarcane aphid) spread the virus; infected seed cane carries it to new fields.
symptoms: Bright yellow midrib on the underside of older leaves
Yellowing spreads into the blade from the midrib
Leaves dry from the tip; canes short and thin

steps.title: Mark yellowed stools
steps.instruction: Note where plants with yellow midribs are.

steps.title: Use virus-free seed cane
steps.instruction: Plant tissue-culture or certified setts next time.
steps.rationale: Breaks the chain of infected seed.

steps.title: Control aphids where advised
steps.instruction: Follow local advice on aphid control.

lifecycle: Aphids feed on an infected plant.
They carry the virus to healthy canes.
Midribs of older leaves turn yellow.
Infected seed cane spreads it to new fields.
